title: Recipe 30 — Sandboxed Code Execution (the isolation boundary is a container, not a process)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Python, JavaScript and Shell as real tools — running network=none, read-only root, on a pinned image allow-list.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed showcase spec is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — only the last beat needs it.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the spec that opts into sandboxed tools

beats.label: Type the plainest agent
beats.cue: “Start from the plainest agent. It has no code execution, and that is the safe default — you have to opt in.”

beats.label: Open the tools list
beats.cue: “Tools are a top-level block. Watch the names: the spec key is camelCase, the model-facing tool is PascalCase.”

beats.label: Add the code-execution trio
beats.cue: “python, javascript, shell — one image each: python:3.13-slim, node:22-alpine, alpine:3.19.”

beats.label: Open the permissions block
beats.cue: “All three declare requiresSandbox: true, so without a grant they are denied outright. mode: default is not enough.”

beats.label: Allow the trio — and read why
beats.cue: “The showcase's own comment is the argument: always-on, because the boundary is a container. The exact docker run flags are right there in the spec.”

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Clean — three sandboxed tools and their grants, twenty-five lines total.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The tool names lower to their registered forms. Nothing about Docker appears here — the image is chosen per call, at runtime.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli with the three code-execution tools

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, boots it: GREEN with no key and no container running.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate. Also lands live/dist/node_modules/@crewhaus/sandbox, which the next two beats interrogate.

beats.label: Find the sandbox wiring
beats.cue: “Two lines. The tools come from one package, and sandboxAvailable is read off CREWHAUS_SANDBOX — noop is the only value that says no container.”

verify.note: 2 lines — the javascript/python/shell import, and sandboxAvailable derived from CREWHAUS_SANDBOX

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: “Read the sandboxAvailable line out loud. That single boolean is what the permission floor hangs on.”

beats.label: Prove the requiresSandbox floor
beats.cue: “Same engine the runtime uses, and the spec's own alwaysAllow Python rule. With no sandbox it is still denied — a grant cannot lift the floor.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const y=Bun.YAML.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("live/crewhaus.yaml","utf8")); const {evaluateWithReason}=await import("./live/dist/node_modules/@crewhaus/permission-engine/dist/index.js"); const rs={flag:[],settings:[],yaml:y.permissions.rules.map(r=>({...r,source:"yaml"})),hooks:[],builtin:[]}; const call={toolName:"Python",input:{code:"print(2+2)"},readOnly:false,destructive:true,requiresSandbox:true}; const a=evaluateWithReason(call,"default",rs); const b=evaluateWithReason(call,"default",rs,{sandboxAvailable:true}); console.log("alwaysAllow Python, no sandbox -> "+a.decision+" — "+a.reason); console.log("alwaysAllow Python, sandbox up -> "+b.decision); if(a.decision!=="deny"||b.decision!=="allow") throw new Error("the sandbox floor moved")'

verify.note: deny with the requiresSandbox reason when sandboxAvailable is false (what CREWHAUS_SANDBOX=noop produces); allow once a real backend is wired

beats.label: Try to run an off-list image
beats.cue: “The allow-list is checked before anything is spawned — so this refusal needs no Docker at all. A buggy tool cannot pull an arbitrary image.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const {createSandbox,SANDBOX_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_IMAGES}=await import("./live/dist/node_modules/@crewhaus/sandbox/dist/index.js"); console.log("curated default allow-list: "+SANDBOX_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_IMAGES.join(", ")); const sb=createSandbox({allowedImages:["python:3.13-slim"]}); const run=sb.exec.bind(sb); try{ await run({image:"attacker/evil:latest",argv:["sh","-c","echo pwned"]}); throw new Error("an off-list image was NOT refused"); }catch(e){ if(!/allowlist/.test(e.message)) throw e; console.log("refused: "+e.message); }'

verify.note: prints the curated default list, then `refused: image "attacker/evil:latest" is not on the allowlist — allowed: python:3.13-slim`. Hermetic: the allow-list check precedes the container spawn, so no container runtime is needed.

beats.label: List the registered images
beats.cue: “The section-18 trio auto-registers. Without --probe nothing is run, so every image reads as not yet probed — that is the honest answer, not a green tick.”

verify.note: three bullets — javascript node:22-alpine, python python:3.13-slim, shell alpine:3.19, all `not yet probed`

beats.label: Probe every image for real
beats.cue: [manual] “--probe constructs a sandbox and runs each image's healthcheck argv. A tick means the image pulled and answered.”

verify.note: needs a container runtime up, so it is not hermetic and cannot be an offline beat (CI has no Docker). Verified locally with Docker running: all three flip to ✓ with a lastHealthyAt, exit 0. Add --format json for the raw status objects.

groups.title: One more thing · the polyglot registry, and a real run

beats.label: Type the recipe's eighth language
beats.cue: “Adding a language is a leaf change: an id, an image, an entrypoint, a healthcheck. runtime-core never learns about Go.”

beats.label: Run the registry smoke
beats.cue: “Seven probes over exactly that pattern — register, look up, reject a bad id, drive the healthchecks. No Docker, no key.”

verify.note: probes A–G green, ALL PROBES PASSED. This is one of the two offline smokes the recipe now names (the other is smoke/section-30-smoke); the broken `smoke:section-18` script has been removed from package.json.

beats.label: Ask the agent to compute in the sandbox
beats.cue: [needs-key] “One turn, one Python call. The code runs in a container with no network and a read-only root — and the answer comes back as a tool result.”
beats.command: crewhaus run live/crewhaus.yaml --prompt "Use the Python tool to compute the 30th Fibonacci number, then tell me just the number."

verify.note: needs Anthropic credentials AND a container runtime up (Docker or podman); --prompt runs a single turn and exits, so there is no REPL to close
